Render several MIDIs in one go, pick up a stopped render where it left off, and play 31-EDO and other microtonal tunings.

## Before you upgrade

- **A render now writes `name.partial.wav` while it runs** and takes its real name when it's whole, so a render that stops never leaves something that looks finished. A program that waits for the output file should wait for that. `--no-resume` writes straight to the output name instead.
- **SFZ regions with no `pitch_keycenter` sound different, because they were wrong.** They played five octaves too high whenever their sample carried a `smpl` chunk. They're rooted on key 60 now, the way BASSMIDI does it.

## What's new

- **Several MIDIs at once.** `kestrel --force-cli render a.mid b.mid c.mid -s gm.sf2 -o renders/` makes a file for each, and `kestrel --force-cli batch jobs.json` gives each MIDI its own soundfonts. In the guided renderer, pick several MIDIs and give each a soundfont set from a table you drive with the arrow keys. Each file is byte-for-byte what that MIDI renders as on its own. The API has `batch` too. See [docs/batch.md](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/blob/main/docs/batch.md).
- **Resume a stopped render.** A render saves its progress every 10 minutes and when you stop it, to a `.krsm` file beside the output. `kestrel --force-cli resume file.krsm`, or **Resume a render** in the guided renderer's menu, goes on from there, and the file it writes is byte-for-byte the one an uninterrupted render writes. It works for one file and for per-track renders, and the API has `resume`.
- **Stop without keeping a resume file.** Press **Ctrl+C, then Ctrl+D** in the guided renderer, or start with `--no-resume`. A checkpoint of a big render is big, about 1.6 GiB at 16 million voices. The API's `cancel` takes `"discard": true`.
- **31-EDO and other tunings.** `--edo 31` (or 19, 22, 53, anything from 1 to 1200) gives every key a pitch of its own, and the sample that plays is the one recorded nearest it. `--scala` and `--kbm` read Scala scales and keyboard maps. `--31edo` plays MIDIs written for the 31-EDO template. Scale/octave tuning messages in a MIDI are read now, and `--mts-notes` applies single-note tuning changes and bulk dumps. See the README.
- **Very high voice counts are safer on Windows.** A block of millions of voices on a slower card can take over the 2 seconds Windows allows, which resets the graphics driver and ends the render. Kestrel now cuts such a block into pieces, for no change in the output and no cost at the defaults. The crash report says when it looks like a driver reset.
- **The voices step is honest about your card.** It offers the lower of what one GPU buffer binds and what the card's memory holds, and says which. A bigger number still works, with a warning.
- **Per-track renders with many tracks are faster:** 11% on a 137-stem file.
- **After a render, the guided renderer offers Home,** so you can switch to a different kind of render without restarting it.
- **FalconEye.** The machine report tests each GPU in a process of its own, so a driver that crashes the test leaves a report saying so. It leaves out other programs' crash reports and no longer names another program in the Linux kernel log. `kestrel.exe`'s file description is just "Kestrel" now, so Task Manager should name both of its processes that.

## Fixes

- **Two numbers at the voices step disagreed.** The guided renderer offered a "device max" that the next step then refused, without saying why. It follows your flags now, and says what moved it.
- **A device that couldn't be opened said only "Parent device is lost".** It now names the adapter and the backend and says why, and what else to try.
- **The GPU self-test talked about Windows on Linux.** It no longer does.

## If a render fails

Send the log from `logs` (the guided renderer shows its path). If you can, make a machine report too (Extras → Machine report) and send it privately, not in a public issue.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `kestrel-1.3.0-windows-x64.zip` | Windows 10/11 |
| `kestrel-1.3.0-macos-universal.dmg` | macOS 11 or newer (Apple silicon and Intel) |
| `kestrel-1.3.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) |

- **Windows:** unzip and double-click `kestrel.exe`. If SmartScreen warns you, click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** copy `kestrel` out of the dmg. The first time you open it, allow it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.
- **Linux:** extract it and run `./kestrel` in a terminal. You need a Vulkan driver.

Each download has a GitHub attestation proving it was built from this repository. With the GitHub CLI, `gh attestation verify <file> --repo thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi` checks it.

The macOS build hasn't been tested yet. If you try it, please [open an issue](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/issues) and tell us how it went.
